newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Utilicorp NZ withdraws Power NZ offer.
newsitem.headline: Utilicorp NZ withdraws Power NZ offer.

text.p: Utilicorp New Zealand, a unit of Utilicorp United Inc said on Tuesday it had withdrawn a takeover offer dated September 20, 1996, for shares in Power New Zealand.
Utilicorp also wrote to the district councils of South Waikato, Thames-Coromandel, Matamata-Piako and Hauraki, withdrawing an offer dated September 17 for their Power NZ shares.
That offer was effectively superseded by an offer made on November 19, which still stands.
Utilicorp NZ also said on Tuesday it had withdrawn an offer made on May 14, 1996, to WEL Energy Group Ltd and its nominees, for their shares in Power New Zealand.
The Thames-Coromandel, Matamata-Piako, South Waikato and Hauraki district councils own 7.1 percent of Power NZ.
Earlier, Auckland-based Mercury Energy Ltd said it had withdrawn all offers for shares in Power New Zealand. Mercury had been waging a long-running battle with Utilicorp NZ over the Power NZ shares.
Utilicorp NZ is 79 percent owned by Utilicorp United Inc.
Power NZ shares were untraded following the announcements, after closing on Monday at NZ$8.05.
Mercury, for more than two years, has been locked in a battle with Kansas-based UtiliCorp for control of its fellow Auckland electricity distributor.
Mercury has around 31 percent of Power NZ while Utilicorp, through Utilicorp New Zealand Ltd, around 28 percent.
Spokesmen for all three parties were not immediately available for comment on the latest developments.
